deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is the verso of a short covering note, written in very faded ink and largely illegible. It is not by Riemann. It is signed 'Ergebenst' (respectfully) by K. Hattendorff, who edited Riemann's minimal-surface paper.

What can be made out with reasonable confidence:
- About five lines of text, which appear to be editorial or printing instructions. They seem to cite page and line references ('S. 6', 'Zeile', ordinal numbers such as '1te' and '8te'). They seem to ask that something be altered or exchanged ('statt ...'), and they appear to mention corrections or remarks for the printed version.
- A closing formula, 'Ergebenst'.
- A place and date line. It is probably '... Aug. 1876' rather than 18[?]. 1876 is the year Riemann's Gesammelte Werke appeared, edited by H. Weber with Dedekind.
- The signature, 'K. Hattendorff'.
- Below these there are faint stamp or pencil traces and offset dirt. None of it carries mathematical content.

Context: the next page (55) is Hattendorff's prefatory note for the second printing of the minimal-surface paper in the Werke. That note explains that Riemann's 1860-61 formula-only manuscript was given to Hattendorff in April 1866. Hattendorff submitted the worked-up paper to the Göttingen Gesellschaft on 6 Jan 1867, and it was printed in Abhandlungen vol. 13. The note also refers to Weierstrass's 1866 Berlin Monatsberichte paper.

This folio is therefore editorial correspondence accompanying that preface or the revised text. It contains no derivations to reconstruct.

results.what: Editorial cover note by K. Hattendorff concerning the reprint of Riemann's minimal-surface memoir (probably for the 1876 Gesammelte Werke)
